name: Rank Forge – SEO Score, Schema, Sitemap & Redirects
author: avakodeforge

sections.description:
Rank Forge is a modern SEO plugin built around a single insight: an SEO score is only useful if it tells you exactly what to do next. The post-edit metabox gives you a 0-100 SEO score, a SERP preview, focus-keyword analysis, and an editable meta title / description / schema — all from one screen, with no account or API key required.

Everything in the Free plugin happens on your own site: schema markup, XML sitemap, robots.txt, the redirect + 404 manager, image SEO (auto alt text), local business schema, and video schema. The only requests it makes are the two listed under External services: the Broken Links scan, when you start it, and the check of your own site’s robots.txt. The optional Pro add-on layers AI on top — one-click AI meta generation, content optimization, and schema detection — plus Google Search Console, Site Audit, A/B testing and auto internal links.

Free

  • On-page SEO score (0-100) per post
  • SERP preview
  • Focus keyword analysis
  • XML sitemap
  • robots.txt editor
  • Basic schema markup (Article, BlogPosting) and the visual Schema Builder
  • Noindex / nofollow per post
  • Redirect manager (301, 302, 307) with 404 log
  • Broken-link scanner across all published content (SSRF-pinned for safety)
  • Image SEO — automatic alt text and a bulk no-alt report
  • Local Business schema (LocalBusiness / NAP / opening hours)
  • Video SEO — VideoObject schema and a video sitemap
  • Coexists with Yoast / Rank Math / AIOSEO / SEOPress during migration

Rank Forge Pro

Pro is a separate add-on plugin, distributed from https://rankforgewp.com and not
included in this download. Everything listed above is part of this plugin and
works without it.

  • AI meta generation (title, description, focus keyword)
  • AI content expansion / simplification / external-link suggestions
  • Internal link suggestions and automatic internal linking
  • Google Search Console integration (rankings, indexing requests)
  • Site audit (your 200 most recent published posts and pages, checked for missing titles, descriptions, headings and alt text, thin content and duplicate titles; with WooCommerce, also your 200 most recent products, checked for titles, descriptions, focus keywords, alt text and duplicate titles)
  • Content brief, content decay and the content optimizer
  • A/B testing for titles + descriptions
  • Priority email support with an active Pro licence

Part of the Forge Suite: twelve WordPress and WooCommerce plugins by Avakode, including Lang Forge, Form Forge and Field Forge.

External services

Rank Forge can make outbound HTTP requests. Nothing is sent until you use the feature that sends it: activating the plugin does not contact any server and does not schedule anything that would. This is the whole list: the plugin’s code makes no other request. Each one is an ordinary WordPress HTTP request, so the server it reaches sees the network address it came from.

  • The sites your content links to — only when you start a Broken Links scan (Rank Forge → Tools → Broken Links), the plugin sends a HEAD request to each link found in your published content to see whether it still answers. The request carries WordPress’s standard user-agent, which names your site’s address; nothing else about your site or your visitors is sent, and nothing is checked until you start the scan.
  • Your own site’s robots.txt — only when an administrator opens a Rank Forge screen that shows the status of robots.txt (Settings, Robots.txt), the plugin fetches /robots.txt at your own site’s address with a plain GET, no body and no credentials, to show what visitors and crawlers receive; the answer is kept for 60 seconds. The request goes to your own site, carries WordPress’s standard user-agent (which names your site’s address), and nothing is sent to any other server.

Search Console, Analytics and Indexing, and the AI features, belong to the separate Rank Forge Pro add-on, which describes the services it uses in its own documentation. This plugin has no analytics, no telemetry and no licensing calls of its own.
sections.installation:
1. Upload rankforge to /wp-content/plugins/, or install via Plugins → Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open any post / page — the Rank Forge metabox appears below the editor.
  4. (Optional) The AI features, Search Console, Site Audit and the other Pro screens come with the separate Rank Forge Pro add-on; the add-on adds its own Connect screen.
sections.faq:
Will Rank Forge conflict with Yoast or Rank Math?

No. Rank Forge detects the active SEO plugin and suppresses its own meta output until you fully migrate. Use Rank Forge → Migration when ready.

Does the SEO score use AI?

The score itself is deterministic (keyword density, readability, internal links, image alt, etc.). AI is only used for generation actions (meta, schema, content expansion) when you click “Generate with AI”.

How are redirects stored?

In a custom table (wp_rankforge_redirects) — not in wp_options like some plugins. This avoids the autoload-bloat that hurts your TTFB.

1.4.0

  • Fixed: keep the uninstall choice compatible with older Free versions when only one package has been updated.
  • Needs Rank Forge Pro 1.2.5 or newer if you run the add-on, as before.
  • Uninstall keeps analyses, redirects, SEO metadata and settings unless “Delete Rank Forge data on uninstall” is selected. Google connection credentials are always removed.
  • Removed unused Freemius integration code.

1.3.0

  • Needs Rank Forge Pro 1.2.5 or newer if you run the add-on, as before.
  • Broken Links: the scan now covers every published post (it used to read only the first 200). It works through them in small background jobs that carry on from one another and it runs by itself once a night. A scan that stopped before the end says “The last scan did not finish” and how far it got, a second press while a scan runs does not start another one, a link used in many posts is checked once per scan, and a link whose address has no host counts as broken.
  • Broken Links: a link is no longer called broken when the check could not tell. A link whose host name could not be looked up right now, or that this server has no route to (often an IPv6-only host on a server without IPv6), is skipped and tried again at the next scan; a site that cannot check addresses safely (it needs the PHP cURL extension and no proxy server) says so instead of calling those links unreachable.
  • Broken Links: each check looks the host name up once, goes ahead only when every address it gets is public, and connects to exactly those addresses. Links to local, private and other non-public addresses are skipped, now including the 100.64.0.0/10 and 198.18.0.0/15 ranges and IPv4 addresses written inside IPv6.
  • Sitemap: password-protected posts, and posts whose canonical address points to another page, are left out of the maps and the index. A post whose canonical is written in another percent-encoding (a Cyrillic address, for example) stays in. The Video sitemap takes its description from the excerpt and then the title, and leaves out protected posts and posts with a canonical elsewhere.
  • Sitemap: a site set to discourage search engines has no sitemap and robots.txt names none; Settings no longer links to a sitemap that would answer 404. A map the index does not announce answers 404 and is not cached.
  • Sitemap: the addresses also work on sites with plain permalinks, the index answers right after the plugin is activated, and deactivating the plugin removes the rewrite rules of the maps.
  • Sitemap: the cached maps are dropped when a post’s noindex, canonical, video data or featured image is written by any means (an import, WP-CLI, the REST API), and when you change the “Show in search results” switch of a post type or the URL limit, not only when a post is saved. A bulk change drops them once.
  • robots.txt: the physical robots.txt file that Rank Forge wrote is removed when the plugin is deactivated or deleted, only if it is still what Rank Forge wrote. The sitemap line is added unless your text already has the index line (a line for some other map no longer stands in for it), and the warning shown when robots.txt could not be written is printed again.
  • Redirects: the automatic redirect made when a post’s address changes uses the old address as it was, and the full 404 log takes a new frequent address instead of ignoring it.
  • Redirects: a target that a browser would read as another site is no longer saved or followed: http:/other.example, http:other.example, // with no host, /\other.example, or an address with a tab or a line break inside. A target written as //other.example/page is an address on another host, so it needs “Allow redirect to external domain”. Rules whose target is mailto:, tel: or another address that is not a web address no longer fire, and the Redirects list marks them. On a site in a sub-folder such as /blog, the address /blog-post is no longer taken for an address inside the folder.
  • SEO score: the “paragraph over 150 words” check follows one rule in the score and in the live figure in the editor, and the score stored for a post matches the editor’s. Inline tags no longer cut a paragraph in two, a block-level tag or a blank line ends one, as WordPress reads it, so classic-editor posts score like their HTML. A post with no words left once its shortcodes are taken out no longer gets a word count.
  • Image SEO: alt text made from a file name drops the size, the suffixes WordPress adds and its counter, in any order; a short number counts as a counter only after a size or a suffix.
  • Descriptions: the {{excerpt}} variable, the automatic description and the descriptions in the JSON-LD markup take the post text without its shortcodes instead of printing them as literal text, and a post that is one shortcode pair from start to end gets no description tag.
  • The page <title> is escaped the same way as the meta title tag (Yoast still gets the raw text).
  • Meta generation: when the AI was asked and did not answer, the stored SEO title and description stay as they were and the editor says so; the preview no longer offers a plain title as if the AI had written it.
  • Schema: WooCommerce’s own BreadcrumbList is dropped where Rank Forge prints one, as its Product markup already was. sameAs and openingHours of the Local Business markup are lists without empty items.
  • Schema Builder: text in a script other than Latin (Russian, Greek, Arabic, Hindi and so on) in the forms of FAQ, Product, HowTo and the other types was stored as a row of codes like u041f…, and quotes and backslashes were lost. The data is now saved the way WordPress expects it. Entries saved before stay as they are: open the post, type the text in the form again and save to repair it.
  • Other SEO plugins: Rank Math’s description, robots, social tags and schema and Yoast’s robots and schema are taken off while Rank Forge is active, and WordPress’s own robots rules for search results and embeds stay in place when Rank Math clears them. AIOSEO is handled through its own filters, and the description it adds to a home page tagline is cut out of its block so the page keeps one description. SEOPress’s social tags are removed by name, only the ones Rank Forge prints itself (fb:app_id, fb:admins, twitter:site, twitter:creator, og:locale and article:* stay).
  • Other SEO plugins: their search engine verification codes are kept, and the canonical of another plugin or of WordPress is removed only on a page where Rank Forge prints one, so an attachment keeps the canonical of WordPress, Lang Forge or Yoast.
  • Import from another SEO plugin: when the import is not set to overwrite, it fills only empty fields and never clears noindex; the source’s title separator is carried over; a post that already has a title of ours is no longer skipped whole, the title stays and the empty fields are filled. AIOSEO’s tags are replaced in their real #name form, and the ones Rank Forge cannot fill are dropped with the text between them kept.
  • Sites that came from SEO Forge: a leftover _seoforge_ row no longer doubles a live _rankforge_ field, and a one-time repair merges the rows that were doubled. It works through the posts in small windows under a lock and marks itself done only after a clean pass over all of them.
  • Deleting the plugin now also removes the term meta of categories and tags (noindex, nofollow, meta title and description), the Google Analytics property you chose and its label, the Search Console and Analytics connection flags, the Broken Links scan data and the flags of the rename repair. The robots.txt file Rank Forge wrote is removed too (only if it is still what Rank Forge wrote), also when the plugin is deleted while it is still active.
  • Deactivating the plugin no longer leaves the hourly statistics event on the schedule, whether or not you agreed to usage statistics.
  • New and reworded sentences are translated in all 15 languages.

The plugin used to buffer the entire head output between two hooks so competing canonical tags could be stripped from it; that buffer is gone. WordPress core’s canonical is still suppressed while a per-post custom canonical is set, and Yoast’s through its filter, so the URL you set is still the one that ships.

1.1.1

The rule used to apply to every filename WordPress touched, and it stripped non-Latin scripts entirely — a file named in Russian, Japanese or Greek came out as a timestamp. Accented Latin now transliterates, and a name that leaves nothing behind is kept as WordPress sanitised it. Add ‘image_filename_cleanup’ => false to the settings to turn it off.

  • The plugin is now called Rank Forge. Nothing about what it does has changed; the name did.
  • Everything the old name stored is carried over on first load: the analysis, redirect and breadcrumb tables, every setting, and the SEO fields on every post. Redirects keep working, stored analyses stay, and the meta on your posts stays. If the takeover is interrupted it resumes on the next request rather than half-applying.
  • Scheduled jobs left under the old names are unscheduled, and the old cached values are dropped so they regenerate under the new ones.

1.0.40

  • Removed the last licence checks that stood over code shipped in this download. The settings screen asked the licence before writing two flags, “auto_meta” and “internal_links_enabled” — neither was ever read by anything, …

short_description: SEO score, meta, schema and sitemap for WordPress: meta box, SERP preview, robots.txt, redirects, image SEO. A Yoast-compatible SEO plugin.
description:
Rank Forge is a modern SEO plugin built around a single insight: an SEO score is only useful if it tells you exactly what to do next. The post-edit metabox gives you a 0-100 SEO score, a SERP preview, focus-keyword analysis, and an editable meta title / description / schema — all from one screen, with no account or API key required.

Everything in the Free plugin happens on your own site: schema markup, XML sitemap, robots.txt, the redirect + 404 manager, image SEO (auto alt text), local business schema, and video schema. The only requests it makes are the two listed under External services: the Broken Links scan, when you start it, and the check of your own site’s robots.txt. The optional Pro add-on layers AI on top — one-click AI meta generation, content optimization, and schema detection — plus Google Search Console, Site Audit, A/B testing and auto internal links.

Free

  • On-page SEO score (0-100) per post
  • SERP preview
  • Focus keyword analysis
  • XML sitemap
  • robots.txt editor
  • Basic schema markup (Article, BlogPosting) and the visual Schema Builder
  • Noindex / nofollow per post
  • Redirect manager (301, 302, 307) with 404 log
  • Broken-link scanner across all published content (SSRF-pinned for safety)
  • Image SEO — automatic alt text and a bulk no-alt report
  • Local Business schema (LocalBusiness / NAP / opening hours)
  • Video SEO — VideoObject schema and a video sitemap
  • Coexists with Yoast / Rank Math / AIOSEO / SEOPress during migration

Rank Forge Pro

Pro is a separate add-on plugin, distributed from https://rankforgewp.com and not
included in this download. Everything listed above is part of this plugin and
works without it.

  • AI meta generation (title, description, focus keyword)
  • AI content expansion / simplification / external-link suggestions
  • Internal link suggestions and automatic internal linking
  • Google Search Console integration (rankings, indexing requests)
  • Site audit (your 200 most recent published posts and pages, checked for missing titles, descriptions, headings and alt text, thin content and duplicate titles; with WooCommerce, also your 200 most recent products, checked for titles, descriptions, focus keywords, alt text and duplicate titles)
  • Content brief, content decay and the content optimizer
  • A/B testing for titles + descriptions
  • Priority email support with an active Pro licence

Part of the Forge Suite: twelve WordPress and WooCommerce plugins by Avakode, including Lang Forge, Form Forge and Field Forge.

External services

Rank Forge can make outbound HTTP requests. Nothing is sent until you use the feature that sends it: activating the plugin does not contact any server and does not schedule anything that would. This is the whole list: the plugin’s code makes no other request. Each one is an ordinary WordPress HTTP request, so the server it reaches sees the network address it came from.

  • The sites your content links to — only when you start a Broken Links scan (Rank Forge → Tools → Broken Links), the plugin sends a HEAD request to each link found in your published content to see whether it still answers. The request carries WordPress’s standard user-agent, which names your site’s address; nothing else about your site or your visitors is sent, and nothing is checked until you start the scan.
  • Your own site’s robots.txt — only when an administrator opens a Rank Forge screen that shows the status of robots.txt (Settings, Robots.txt), the plugin fetches /robots.txt at your own site’s address with a plain GET, no body and no credentials, to show what visitors and crawlers receive; the answer is kept for 60 seconds. The request goes to your own site, carries WordPress’s standard user-agent (which names your site’s address), and nothing is sent to any other server.

Search Console, Analytics and Indexing, and the AI features, belong to the separate Rank Forge Pro add-on, which describes the services it uses in its own documentation. This plugin has no analytics, no telemetry and no licensing calls of its own.
